terms.definition: Renunciation of the results of all actions. In BG 12.11, this is the prescription for those impeded from direct devotional service. Hacker metaphor: Like setting up a firewall that blocks outgoing packets of desire for results, redirecting energy toward neutral or noble causes.

Situated in the self; one who has attained inner stability and self-mastery. The verse promises that through renunciation of results, one becomes yatātmavān. Hacker metaphor: Like achieving a stable root filesystem where the kernel operates securely without constant crashes or interrupts.

Taking refuge, seeking shelter. In the verse, it refers to taking refuge in devotional service (mad-yogam). Hacker metaphor: Like a process that, when unable to run its primary service, switches to a safe fallback mode that maintains core functionality.

Consistent, repeated practice. In BG 12.9, Arjuna is advised to follow the regulative principles of bhakti‑yoga (abhyāsa‑yoga) when direct fixation of the mind fails. Hacker metaphor: Like setting a cron job to run a system health check every hour—automated, persistent effort that gradually corrects drift and maintains stability.

Desire, aspiration, longing. The verse promises that through practice, one develops icchā to attain Me. Hacker metaphor: Like a background service that, once initialized, continuously polls for the Divine signal and triggers the devotional process when the connection is strong enough.

Epithet of Arjuna meaning “winner of wealth.” Here it reminds us that the true wealth to be won is not material prosperity but the riches of devotion—Kṛṣṇa Himself. Hacker metaphor: Like achieving root access not to a material server but to the supreme repository of spiritual knowledge, where the real assets are grace and love.

Today’s yoga (until evening), often considered inauspicious, associated with obstacles and delays. Hacker metaphor: Like encountering a intermittent network packet loss that requires retry mechanisms and error‑correcting codes to maintain a reliable connection to the Divine.

Tomorrow’s nakṣatra, meaning “root.” Symbolizes the foundation, the source, and the transformative power that dissolves the superficial to reveal the essential. Hacker metaphor: Like performing a filesystem check (fsck) that identifies and repairs corrupted inodes, allowing the system to mount securely on its true foundation.
lordship, divine power.

The new moon; the day when the moon is not visible, the complete waning. From ama (together) + vāsya (dwelling) — the day when sun and moon dwell together in the same lunar mansion. The void is not empty — it is a convergence.
without beginning or end; infinite in all directions, like an unbounded memory address space
Without division or deviation. The state of single-pointed devotion where the mind admits no rival object. This is not partial commitment — it is the full signal, zero noise.
with these alone.

Today's nakṣatra (until 02:22 AM), ruled by Mitra (god of friendship and alliance). Symbolizes devotion through harmonious connection and balanced relationships. Hacker metaphor: Like a stable, peer-to-peer network node that maintains reliable connection to the Divine server through mutual trust and protocol.
"the effulgence of the great soul"; bhāsaḥ denotes active, self-luminous radiance intrinsic to the Lord's being, not external light.

Intelligence, discrimination, judgment. The verse asks us to invest this buddhi in Me — not just to think about God, but to employ our discriminative faculty in His service. Hacker metaphor: Like allocating your best debugging skills to trace the source code of reality back to the Divine programmer.
eyes.
I give.

"terrible teeth"; the gaping, dreadful teeth of the universal form. Time devours all forms — like a debug trace exposing every hidden dependency, the cosmic form reveals what is truly permanent and what is only structural overlay.
in the body.
"Lord of lords"; the title asserting Krishna's supremacy over every other being. All demigods tremble before this form; Arjuna bypasses them and goes directly to the source.
"fixed, immovable"; the pole star yoga. Maps onto puruṣa in Sāṅkhya: never moves, never changes, the fixed reference for all movement.

the hypothetical magnitude that would still fall short of the universal form's effulgence. Sanskrit uses the conditional mood deliberately: the comparison is an approximation offered by language's limitations.
divine, supernatural.
“I give you divine eyes”; the granting of higher perception by grace; not earned by effort alone but given to the qualified devotee.
to see, to behold.
to see, to behold.
blazing with fires of knowledge; the process that burns away karma through transcendental understanding
O Arjuna (epithet meaning "lord of sleep" or "one with thick hair").

"master of all senses"; acknowledges that the hṛṣīka — senses and mind — belong to Īśvara. When recognized, the senses stop running wild and become instruments of bhakti. Equivalent to reclaiming root access from a compromised process.
you wish, you desire.
in one place.

"refuge of the worlds"; the abiding home of all existence. Every temporary refuge — army, skill, status, relationship — belongs to the jagat, the moving world that passes. Krishna alone is its nivāsa.
universe, world.

"the fire of time / death"; the impartial, automatic dissolution of all constructed forms. Not random destruction but the operating system of the material world. Recognising this is realism, not morbidity.
complete, whole, entire.
The great-souled one; He whose self encompasses all selves. Not just "great" but the very definition of greatness as a quality of spirit.

The mind — the faculty that thinks, feels, and wills. In BG 12.8, Arjuna is told to fix this very mind on Kṛṣṇa. Hacker metaphor: Like setting the CPU's instruction pointer to a sacred address — all processing cycles then serve the Divine process.
Attached to Me, devoted to Me. Mat = to Me; parāḥ = attached/having gone to. The devotee whose entire orientation has shifted toward Kṛṣṇa — not as a hobby, not as a practice, but as identity.
Jewel, crystal, gem; that which reflects without altering.
O Me.
Me.
never.
Without delay, very soon. The Lord's promise of swift deliverance. Not 'eventually' — 'quickly'. When surrender is complete, the response is immediate.
“You cannot see Me with your present eyes”; the acknowledgment of the limitation of ordinary vision; spiritual equivalent of a hardware upgrade requirement.
"the ninth"; Kṛṣṇa Pakṣa Navamī marks the final threshold before Amāvāsyā. Completion energy: finish what needs finishing.
supreme resting place, ultimate refuge; the divine base that supports all existence, like the foundation of a terminal server cluster
see, behold.
“Behold My mystic opulence!”; the invitation to see the Lord’s divine powers and manifestations; the opulence (aiśvarya) is the inconceivable powers of the Supreme.

"by the glories, by recounting"; the mechanism of transformation. The Lord's glories are active — they reorganize reality around themselves. Demons recoil; perfected beings advance. The glories do not convert; they reveal.
terms.roots: from pra + √kṛ, "to do thoroughly, to accomplish" — the thorough act of revealing

terms.definition: "be gracious, show favor"; the central devotional cry of the verse. Not a demand for outcomes, but a request for restoration after confusion. Recognised helplessness is the precondition for every genuine spiritual breakthrough.
the Supreme Person; the conscious witness that runs the simulation
"demons, rākṣasas"; inner patterns of defending a false identity. When truth is spoken, they flee. Not external beings to be destroyed but the structural overlay of ego that cannot tolerate reality.
terms.roots: from rakṣas, "to protect, to guard" — the demons are those who guard the false self

terms.definition: Aldebaran, α Tauri, the red giant 44× the Sun's diameter. Prajāpati's creative, generative nakṣatra; the fixed brilliant star of manifestation.
moving and non-moving.
"absorption, coalescence." The mind becomes transparent and takes on the color of its object. Direct perceptual transformation, not fantasy-visualization.

Surrendering, giving up, relinquishing. Not passive renunciation but active offering — placing everything at the Lord's feet as an act of service. Like deploying code with zero local backups — total trust.

Beautiful, gentle form; the most beautiful form. Saumya derives from soma (the lunar essence, the nectar of tranquility). This is not just "pretty" — it is the form that calms the mind and restores the heart.
terms.roots: from soma (the lunar essence, the nectar of tranquility)

terms.definition: The ocean of material existence (saṁsāra). Called an ocean because it is vast, deep, and terrifyingly easy to drown in. The Lord does not teach you to swim better — He pulls you out.

"the assembled perfected beings"; those whose citta is purified and who immediately recognize the Lord. Their bowing is not new devotion — it is the consummation of lifelong orientation. Like code that finally compiles after years of debugging.
Lion; the sovereign beast, symbol of royalty, fearlessness, and dharma.

"rightly, fitly, appropriately"; Arjuna's assessment that the Lord's actions are correct in every instance. The culmination of discriminative knowledge — not passive acceptance but recognition that the Lord's justice is always precisely calibrated.
with your own eyes.
His own form; the essential, original form of the Supreme, distinct from any manifested cosmic display.

"Then the seer abides in its own form"; the foundational statement of yoga's goal. Svarūpe (in its own form) and avasthānam (abiding) together describe the settled state — not striving, not becoming, simply being what one truly is.
to you.
radiance, luminosity; the API key that illuminates all systems
but.
And divine serpents; uraga = serpent, divya = divine, luminous, shining with inner light.

"the attacker, the obstacle-smasher"; the yoga active today. Vyāghāta smashes everything — valuable and worthless alike. It is not selective. This is why Ekādaśī paired with Vyāghāta is intense: dissolution is non-negotiable.
terms.roots: from √han, "to strike, to smash"; prefix vi- intensifies — thorough, complete striking

terms.definition: The Moon's sign today — Scorpio. Represents transformation, depth, and the courage to face hidden truths. Hacker metaphor: Like a rootkit scan that reveals and removes hidden processes (karmic imprints) that interfere with divine operation.
whatever else.
mystic power, union.
maintainer of the eternal religion; preserves spiritual infrastructure like a version-controlled dharma repository
Encouraged, reassured, restored to calm; the act of dispelling fear. Kṛṣṇa does not just change form — He actively reassures.

"devotion to the Lord"; complete surrender of will and effort to Ishvara. From YS 1.23. Not passive resignation but active dedication, cultivated when the mind is steady so it remains available when the mind is not.

Devotion to the Lord; surrender of the fruits of action to the Divine. This is the practice BG 12.8 enjoins and YS 1.23 highlights as a direct path to samādhi. Hacker metaphor: Like setting up a continuous integration pipeline where every action is automatically tested, built, and deployed in service to the Divine repository.
are able.

"grace, divine shelter"; the specific refuge that only surrender to the Lord provides. Arjuna cannot obtain it while citta is scattered, but the recognition of its absence is precisely the opening for its return.
Renunciation of the fruits of action. In BG 12.12, this is presented as superior to knowledge and meditation for attaining peace of mind.
Peace, tranquility, freedom from disturbance. The verse promises that karma-phala-tyāga leads to śānti.
Consistent spiritual practice. The verse places this as the first step in the graduated approach to spiritual realization.
Today’s nakṣatra (until 08:14 AM), meaning “root.” Symbolizes foundation, origin, and the transformative power that addresses bondage at its source.
